matches.rationale: No finding addresses the inflated FT-HID dataset size (38,364 vs. the true 9,120). Predicted findings only mention a table caption inconsistency for the appendix, not this specific data-integrity issue in the Method section.
Finding pred_id 2 correctly identifies the sign error in the Rodrigues rotation formula (1+cosθ instead of 1−cosθ) in Equation 3, which is the exact corruption described in gt_id 2.

No finding reports the omission of critical training hyperparameters (batch size, learning rate schedule, warmup, weight decay) from Section 4.1. The predicted findings do not mention missing implementation details.
No finding calls out the exaggerated 'first egocentric realistic world simulator' claim in the abstract. The predictions focus on frame rate contradictions, not on false claims of primacy.
The fabricated reference [49] (Matrix-Game) is not mentioned in any finding. None of the predicted issues concern a non-existent citation in the Related Work.
There is no finding that the evaluation was silently restricted to indoor scenes. No predicted error relates to selective scene subset reporting or the omission of outdoor/occluded test cases.

Finding pred_id 3 identifies the introduction of an undefined parameter βt in Equation 1, noting the noise schedule becomes inconsistent with the variance condition. This matches the unexplained β corruption in gt_id 7.

No finding addresses the unbalanced experimental protocol where competitors receive enriched text captions while PlayerOne uses raw motion sequences. The predictions do not mention this asymmetric input bias.

The predicted findings do not challenge the overgeneralized claim of 'consistent superiority in diverse scenarios' based on a limited 100‑video indoor benchmark. No finding matches this overclaim in Section 4.3.
No finding detects the deleted anonymization statement or raises the missing ethical disclosures (IRB, consent). The predictions do not mention Figure 1 caption or ethical omissions.

The promotional rewriting of the Introduction (claiming the method 'completely solves all challenges') is not flagged by any finding. Predicted errors do not include rhetorical inflation in the Introduction.
Finding pred_id 1 directly captures the cross-section inconsistency between the abstract's real‑time/30 FPS claim and Section 4.1’s actual 8 FPS, which is the exact mismatch described in gt_id 12.
No finding notes the fabricated MPJPE value of 98.42 in the ablation table (Table 2) that conflicts with the 127.16 in Table 3. This data manipulation is not among the predicted errors.
The channel‑dimension mismatch (zmotion ∈ R^{k×5×h×w} instead of R^{k×3×h×w}) is not mentioned in any finding. Predicted issues do not flag this inconsistency in the motion latent representation.
No finding identifies the contradiction between the conclusion’s 'ensures coherent world generation' and the documented limitations on game scenarios. This cross‑section overclaim is not detected.
